title: Sam Richardson in “Into the Sky” Debuts at Fantastic Fest
seoTitle: Sam Richardson in “Into the Sky” Debuts at Fantastic Fest
subtitle: The actor stars in a film that explores alien abductions with humor and reflection on denial.
excerpt: Sam Richardson takes center stage with the world premiere of “Into the Sky” at Fantastic Fest 2026, a sci‑fi comedy about recurring alien abductions and personal.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Actor Sam Richardson is in the spotlight after the world premiere of his new film, “Into the Sky”, at Fantastic Fest 2026. The production, described as a science‑fiction thriller with comedy, places Richardson in the role of a man dealing with recurring alien abductions.

The Premiere of “Into the Sky”

“Into the Sky” had its first showing at Fantastic Fest 2026, co‑directed and co‑written by Drew Mylrea and Evan Buxbaum. The film is a comedic sci‑fi thriller that invites the audience to look both upward and inward in equal measure. The plot explores issues such as personal resistance versus agency, love, strength and interpersonal faith, inserting these themes into a unique and unpredictable context.

The Central Plot: Abduction and Denial

At the heart of the story is Bobby, played by Sam Richardson, who for a year has been waking up inexplicably in random places, covered in a blue slime, due to alien abductions. This situation creates tension in his marriage, and after one of the abductions Bobby discovers that his wife, Brittany, has left him and rented out the house. The abductions are portrayed as a physical representation of Bobby’s inability to recognize the problems in his life, with the character treating them as something to get used to or accept rather than to confront or address.

Characters and Relationships in Focus

Bobby’s house is now occupied by Nico, an event organizer played by Sofia Black‑D'Elia, who is stressed about her brother Chance’s marriage to Genevieve. Bobby is not alone in his abduction experiences, meeting Jaden (David Cross), who becomes a counterpoint and mirror for him. Jaden represents an alternate path for Bobby, showing someone who has acknowledged the struggle of living with the abductions. Additionally, Bobby gets involved in an elaborate ruse to help Nico impress her family, posing as a music‑festival producer.

Dialogues with “The X‑Files” and the Genre Balance

“Into the Sky” is clearly inspired by “The X‑Files”, especially episodes that blended the supernatural with humor. The film seeks a balance between the alien‑abduction story and comedy, opting to lean slightly more toward humor. This approach is seen as successful, adding novelty to an abduction story that could otherwise feel familiar. The narrative manages to blend various genres and elements—abduction tale, romance, and the notion of “not being alone”—converging its metaphors effectively.

Praised Performances and Narrative Depth

The cast’s performances are highlighted, with Sam Richardson praised for his versatility and for making Bobby a captivating and charming character. Sofia Black‑D'Elia is also noted as “wonderful” in the role of Nico, and the chemistry between her and Richardson is observed. David Cross, as Jaden, is described as “excellent”, bringing an energy that lifts the scenes. The film explores the feeling that trusted people can abandon someone in the face of an “inconvenient truth”, using abductions as a metaphor for medical conditions or physical changes, and questioning “who are your people?” amid life’s challenges.

With information from Elements of Madness, The HoloFiles.
